lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.unitTitle: Kitchen Care and Basic Food Safety
lessonRef.title: Explicit model: handwashing

objective: Learners watch an adult model the full handwashing sequence (wet, soap, scrub 20 seconds, rinse, dry) with attention to when it matters most in a kitchen, then demonstrate the same sequence correctly on their own twice.
scenario: An adult models proper handwashing at the kitchen sink, explaining not just the steps but when handwashing matters most in a kitchen — before touching food, after touching raw ingredients, after touching the trash. The learner then washes their hands the same way at two different points during a kitchen task.
safetyNotes: Water temperature stays comfortable to the touch, never scalding.

simulationAlternative.description: If access to a kitchen sink isn't available, the learner instead demonstrates the five-step sequence at any available sink (bathroom, utility) and identifies, in writing, the same two kitchen moments when handwashing would matter most.

tasks.directions: Before the model, name one moment during cooking or kitchen cleanup when you think handwashing matters most, and why.

prompts.text: Name the moment and your reasoning.

tasks.directions: Watch your adult model the five-step handwash (wet, soap, scrub 20 seconds, rinse, dry), then do it yourself right after while they check your timing.

prompts.text: I wet my hands before adding soap, not after.
I scrubbed for about 20 seconds, not a quick rinse.
I dried my hands with a clean towel rather than leaving them wet or wiping on clothing.

tasks.directions: During a real kitchen task, wash your hands correctly at two separate moments on your own, without a reminder.

prompts.text: What were your two moments, and what happened right before each one that told you it was time to wash?
Twenty seconds can feel long when you're in a hurry. What's one trick you could use to actually scrub for the full 20 seconds instead of rushing it?

remediation: If the learner rushes the scrub step, reteach by having them scrub while counting out loud or singing a 20-second song, then fade that support once their internal timing improves.
extension: Teach the five-step handwash to a younger sibling or family member, narrating why each step matters, with an adult confirming the teaching is accurate.
